title: Lesson 9: Focused Read-aloud and Retelling, Session 2: Papa, Please Get the Moon for Me
objective: Students will retell major events from the story Papa, Please Get the Moon for Me and describe its central message, using oral discussion, role-play, and independent writing.

what_is_taught.skill: retell major events from a story
describe the central message of a story
use sentence frames to support oral responses
use future tense in oral language
participate in partner talk and turn-and-talk discussions
role-play story events to demonstrate understanding
write words and draw pictures to show story events
use classroom resources (word walls, story boards) to support writing
use respectful collaboration protocols during partner work
reflect on author's purpose for writing a story

student_actions.recognition_identification: identify proper and common nouns by making hand signals
student_actions.oral_production: use future tense orally, participate in turn-and-talk and partner discussions, role-play story events, share ideas about story message and author purpose
student_actions.written_production: write words and draw pictures on response sheets to show story events
student_actions.procedural_application: apply respectful collaboration protocols during role-play and partner talk
student_actions.reasoning_explanation: explain the central message of the story and author's purpose during partner and whole group discussions
student_actions.comprehension_response: retell major story events orally and in writing, describe the central message, respond to questions about story events and message, reflect on author's purpose in writing the story, use sentence frames to support responses, use word wall vocabulary in discussion and writing, use story illustrations as evidence for retelling events, use future tense in oral language to modify a song, use story elements to organize retelling and writing, participate in role-play to demonstrate understanding of story sequence and details

evidence.quote: Remind students that the song is written in present tense, but that yesterday they changed the words to the past tense.
Tell students that today they will sing it in future tense, so they will sing the song as if it will happen tomorrow.
'Use the future tense to say something you will see in the classroom tomorrow.' Model as needed.
Invite students to sing the song in the past tense with you.
Provide specific, positive feedback on their ability to change the song to the future tense.
Say each character name again and invite students to make a 'p' with their hands if the noun is proper, and a 'c' with their hand if the noun is common.
Invite students to turn and talk to an elbow partner: 'What will we track with the Story Elements board today? (major events from the beginning, middle, and end of the story)'
Encourage students to use the sentence frame: 'In the beginning, _____________.'
Cold call on one to two students to share out.
'Who can repeat what your classmate said?'
Encourage students to use the sentence frame: 'In the middle, _______________.'
Cold call on one or two students to share out.
Invite students to Think-Pair-Share with an elbow partner: 'What was the central message of this story? What do you think the author, Eric Carle, was trying to show and tell us about the moon?'
Cold call on two to three students to share out.

Share with students that as in the previous lessons, they will get a chance to show what they know about the major events in Papa, Please Get the Moon for Me by role-playing the beginning, middle, and end.
Invite students to turn and talk with an elbow partner:
Move students into pre-determined pairs and tell them they are going to use the Role-Play protocol to act out the key details of Papa, Please Get the Moon for Me.
Give students specific, positive feedback on their ability to role-play the key details of Papa, Please Get the Moon for Me.
Display the Papa, Please Get the Moon for Me response sheet.
'Use words and pictures to show what happened in the story.'
Invite students to whisper a response into their hands: 'What happened in the beginning of Papa, Please Get the Moon for Me?'
Tell students that they may begin writing their response in the Beginning box.
Repeat this process with the remaining two boxes, Middle and End.
Circulate to support students as they write. Encourage them to use classroom resources (Story Elements board, Word Walls, high-frequency word lists, and alphabet or letter sound combination charts).
Provide specific, positive feedback about students' ability to complete Part III of their response sheets.
Tell students they are now going to consider why the author may have written Papa, Please Get the Moon for Me.
Direct students' attention to the Unit 1 Guiding Question anchor chart and complete the first column with the book title.
'Was this story about the sun, the moon, or both?'
Invite students to turn and talk with an elbow partner:
'Can you say more about that?'
Cold call on two to three students to share out their ideas.
Invite students to sing and do the movements of the 'Sun, Moon, and Stars' Version 2 song as the lesson comes to a close.

teacher_actions.direct_instruction: Models use of future tense in song; models use of sentence frames for retelling story events; models use of word wall vocabulary; models respectful collaboration protocols; models reflection on author’s purpose.
prompts_that_cue_student_response: Use the future tense to say something you will see in the classroom tomorrow.
What will we track with the Story Elements board today?
What happened in the beginning of the story?
Looking at the illustrations for evidence, describe what happened in the middle of the story.
What happened at the end of the story?
What was the central message of this story? What do you think the author was trying to show and tell us about the moon?
How will you show respect toward others during our Role-Play protocol today?
Why do you think the author wrote the book?
Can you say more about that?

scope.breadth: major story events and central message
scope.depth: retelling, role-play, and writing with support

supports.above_level_extend: Encouragement to expand oral responses; cold calling to share ideas; use of sentence frames to scaffold complex responses.
